framework: California data breach notification statute (amended by SB 446, eff. Jan 1, 2026)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted personal information of a California resident (or encrypted data plus the key); SB 446 added a hard 30-day clock from discovery effective Jan 1, 2026, with delay exceptions for law enforcement and scope determination.
what_is_due: Initial notification to California Attorney General
authority: California Attorney General
legal_reference: Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.29 / 1798.82 (as amended by SB 446); CCPA § 1798.150 (private right of action)

framework: Switzerland Federal Act on Data Protection (revised, 2023)
trigger: Data security breach likely to result in a high risk to the data subject's personality or fundamental rights; notice due 'as soon as possible' — no fixed statutory deadline.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)
legal_reference: FADP (nFADP) Art. 24

framework: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (rule pending finalization)
trigger: NOT IN FORCE: CISA states that covered cyber incident and ransomware payment reporting under CIRCIA will not be required until the final rule takes effect. Under the proposed rule a covered entity would report within 72 hours of reasonably believing a covered cyber incident occurred and within 24 hours of making a ransom payment; the final rule may change those figures.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
legal_reference: 6 U.S.C. § 681b; proposed rule 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM published 4 April 2024). Final rule not yet in effect as of 30 September 2026.

framework: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act
trigger: Classification of an ICT-related incident as 'major' under RTS (EU) 2024/1772; initial notification due within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours from awareness.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Financial competent authority (e.g. BaFin, ACPR, AMF, ECB for significant credit institutions)
authority: Financial competent authority (e.g. BaFin, ACPR, AMF, ECB for significant credit institutions)
legal_reference: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 19; RTS/ITS Reg. (EU) 2025/301 and 2025/302 Art. 5

framework: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act
trigger: Classification of an ICT-related incident as 'major' under RTS (EU) 2024/1772; initial notification due within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours from awareness.
what_is_due: Intermediate report or follow-up notification
authority: Financial competent authority (e.g. BaFin, ACPR, AMF, ECB for significant credit institutions)
legal_reference: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 19; RTS/ITS Reg. (EU) 2025/301 and 2025/302 Art. 5

framework: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act
trigger: Classification of an ICT-related incident as 'major' under RTS (EU) 2024/1772; initial notification due within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours from awareness.
what_is_due: Final report (30 days; see the statute for when the period starts)
authority: Financial competent authority (e.g. BaFin, ACPR, AMF, ECB for significant credit institutions)
legal_reference: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 19; RTS/ITS Reg. (EU) 2025/301 and 2025/302 Art. 5

framework: China Data Security Law
trigger: Discovery of data security flaws, vulnerabilities, or incidents; remedial measures required immediately and users/authorities notified 'promptly' — no fixed statutory hour deadline in the DSL itself.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Competent sectoral regulators and public security/cyberspace authorities
legal_reference: DSL Art. 29 (and Network Data Security Management Regulations, eff. Jan 1, 2025)

framework: EU ePrivacy telecom breach notification (Regulation 611/2013)
trigger: Provider of publicly available electronic communications services detects a personal data breach; all breaches are notifiable to the authority regardless of risk.
what_is_due: Initial notification to National regulatory authority / data protection authority for electronic communications
authority: National regulatory authority / data protection authority for electronic communications
legal_reference: Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 4(3); Commission Regulation (EU) No 611/2013 Art. 2

framework: EU ePrivacy telecom breach notification (Regulation 611/2013)
trigger: Provider of publicly available electronic communications services detects a personal data breach; all breaches are notifiable to the authority regardless of risk.
what_is_due: Intermediate report or follow-up notification
authority: National regulatory authority / data protection authority for electronic communications
legal_reference: Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 4(3); Commission Regulation (EU) No 611/2013 Art. 2

framework: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Vendor of personal health records or related entity (non-HIPAA, incl. health apps) discovers a breach of unsecured identifiable health information, including unauthorized disclosures.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
authority: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
legal_reference: 16 CFR Part 318 (amended final rule effective July 29, 2024)

framework: EU General Data Protection Regulation
trigger: Controller becomes aware of a personal data breach; notification required unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Competent national supervisory authority (e.g. CNIL, BfDI, DPC, Garante)
authority: Competent national supervisory authority (e.g. CNIL, BfDI, DPC, Garante)
legal_reference: GDPR Art. 33/34 (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)

framework: GLBA FTC Safeguards Rule breach notification amendment
trigger: Non-banking financial institution discovers a 'notification event' — unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving 500 or more consumers.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
authority: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
legal_reference: 16 CFR § 314.4(j) and § 314.5 (Safeguards Rule, amended 2023, effective May 13, 2024)

framework: HIPAA/HITECH Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Covered entity discovers a breach of unsecured protected health information, presumed reportable unless a low probability of compromise is demonstrated via risk assessment.
what_is_due: Initial notification to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights (HHS OCR)
authority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights (HHS OCR)

framework: Illinois Personal Information Protection Act (note: BIPA imposes consent/retention duties but contains no breach-notification deadline)
trigger: Discovery or notification of a breach of personal information of Illinois residents; no fixed statutory hour deadline ('most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay'); AG notice required for breaches affecting more than 500 residents.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Illinois Attorney General
legal_reference: 815 ILCS 530/10 and 530/12; Biometric Information Privacy Act 740 ILCS 14 (no notification provision)

framework: India CERT-In Cyber Security Directions (April 2022)
trigger: Noticing or being notified of any incident in the mandatory reporting Annexure (data breaches, ransomware, identity theft, etc.) — 6-hour clock from noticing.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
authority: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
legal_reference: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act 2000 (No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In)

framework: Japan Act on the Protection of Personal Information
trigger: Leakage/loss/damage involving sensitive data, financial-harm risk, wrongful intent (e.g. cyberattack), or 1,000+ individuals; preliminary report due 'promptly' (PPC guidance: roughly 3–5 days), so no fixed hour deadline.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC)
legal_reference: APPI Art. 26; Enforcement Rules Arts. 7–8

framework: Japan Act on the Protection of Personal Information
trigger: Leakage/loss/damage involving sensitive data, financial-harm risk, wrongful intent (e.g. cyberattack), or 1,000+ individuals; preliminary report due 'promptly' (PPC guidance: roughly 3–5 days), so no fixed hour deadline.
what_is_due: Final report (30 days; see the statute for when the period starts)
authority: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC)
legal_reference: APPI Art. 26; Enforcement Rules Arts. 7–8

framework: South Korea Personal Information Protection Act
trigger: Awareness of a personal data breach affecting 1,000+ individuals, sensitive/unique identifier data, or breaches from unauthorized external access — 72-hour clock to regulator and individuals.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) / KISA
authority: Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) / KISA
legal_reference: PIPA Art. 34; Enforcement Decree Arts. 39–40 (as amended Sept 2023)

framework: Brazil Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados
trigger: Awareness of a security incident that may entail relevant risk or damage to data subjects; ANPD regulation sets a 3-business-day deadline (expressed here as 72 hours, excluding non-business days).
what_is_due: Initial notification to Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)
authority: Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)
legal_reference: LGPD Art. 48; ANPD Resolution CD/ANPD No. 15/2024 (breach communication regulation)

framework: Mexico Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (2025)
trigger: Security breach at any processing stage that significantly affects data subjects' property or moral rights; the law mandates immediate notification to data subjects but sets no fixed proactive regulator-notification deadline (Secretaría investigates upon verification/complaint).
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno (replaced INAI; private-sector data authority)
legal_reference: LFPDPPP (DOF 20 Mar 2025, in force 21 Mar 2025) Arts. 19–20

framework: EU NIS2 Directive (Network and Information Security)
trigger: Essential or important entity becomes aware of a significant incident (severe operational disruption, financial loss, or considerable damage to others).
what_is_due: Initial notification to National CSIRT or competent authority of each Member State
authority: National CSIRT or competent authority of each Member State
legal_reference: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 23

framework: EU NIS2 Directive (Network and Information Security)
trigger: Essential or important entity becomes aware of a significant incident (severe operational disruption, financial loss, or considerable damage to others).
what_is_due: Intermediate report or follow-up notification
authority: National CSIRT or competent authority of each Member State
legal_reference: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 23

framework: EU NIS2 Directive (Network and Information Security)
trigger: Essential or important entity becomes aware of a significant incident (severe operational disruption, financial loss, or considerable damage to others).
what_is_due: Final report (30 days; see the statute for when the period starts)
authority: National CSIRT or competent authority of each Member State
legal_reference: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 23

framework: New York SHIELD Act / GBL § 899-aa (as amended Dec 2024)
trigger: Discovery of unauthorized access to or acquisition of computerized private information of NY residents; 30-day hard deadline introduced by the December 2024 amendment.
what_is_due: Initial notification to NY Attorney General, Department of State, State Police, and NYDFS (for DFS-regulated entities)
authority: NY Attorney General, Department of State, State Police, and NYDFS (for DFS-regulated entities)
legal_reference: N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law §§ 899-aa / 899-bb (amended eff. Dec 21, 2024)

framework: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (Part 500)
trigger: Covered entity determines a cybersecurity event occurred requiring notice to another regulator, with reasonable likelihood of material harm, or involving ransomware deployment; extortion payments separately reportable within 24 hours with explanation within 30 days.
what_is_due: Initial notification to New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS)
authority: New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS)

framework: New Zealand Privacy Act 2020 (Notifiable Privacy Breaches)
trigger: Belief that a privacy breach has caused or is likely to cause serious harm; statute requires notice 'as soon as practicable' with no fixed deadline, though OPC guidance expects notification within 72 hours.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner (OPC)
legal_reference: Privacy Act 2020 ss. 112–118

framework: Canada Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act
trigger: Breach of security safeguards creating a real risk of significant harm (RROSH); report due 'as soon as feasible' — no fixed statutory deadline.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC)
legal_reference: PIPEDA s. 10.1; Breach of Security Safeguards Regulations (SOR/2018-64)

framework: China Personal Information Protection Law
trigger: Occurrence or likely occurrence of personal information leakage, tampering, or loss; remedial measures and notification required 'immediately' — no fixed statutory hour deadline.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and sectoral departments performing PI protection duties
authority: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and sectoral departments performing PI protection duties
legal_reference: PIPL Art. 57

framework: China National Cybersecurity Incident Reporting Measures / CII Security Protection Regulations
trigger: CII operator identifies a relatively major or higher-grade cybersecurity incident; CIIOs report within 1 hour to the protection department and public security organ (other operators within 4 hours to local CAC).
what_is_due: Initial notification to CII protection departments, public security organs, and CAC
authority: CII protection departments, public security organs, and CAC
legal_reference: Administrative Measures for National Cybersecurity Incident Reporting (eff. Nov 1, 2025); CII Security Protection Regulations Art. 18

framework: China National Cybersecurity Incident Reporting Measures / CII Security Protection Regulations
trigger: CII operator identifies a relatively major or higher-grade cybersecurity incident; CIIOs report within 1 hour to the protection department and public security organ (other operators within 4 hours to local CAC).
what_is_due: Final report (30 days; see the statute for when the period starts)
authority: CII protection departments, public security organs, and CAC
legal_reference: Administrative Measures for National Cybersecurity Incident Reporting (eff. Nov 1, 2025); CII Security Protection Regulations Art. 18

framework: Saudi Arabia Personal Data Protection Law
trigger: Controller becomes aware of a personal data breach/leak/unauthorized access that may harm personal data, data subjects, or conflict with their interests — 72-hour clock to SDAIA.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA)
authority: Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA)
legal_reference: PDPL Art. 20; Implementing Regulation Art. 24

framework: SEC Cybersecurity Disclosure Rule (Form 8-K Item 1.05)
trigger: Registrant determines, without unreasonable delay after discovery, that a cybersecurity incident is material; 4-business-day clock runs from the materiality determination, not discovery. Modelled here as 96 hours from incident declaration, an approximation of four business days: confirm the actual filing date with counsel.
what_is_due: Initial notification to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
authority: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
legal_reference: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106) and Form 8-K Item 1.05

framework: Singapore Personal Data Protection Act (Data Breach Notification)
trigger: Assessment (expected within 30 days) determines a breach is notifiable — significant harm likely, or significant scale (500+ individuals); PDPC notification due within 3 calendar days of that determination.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC)
authority: Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC)
legal_reference: PDPA ss. 26A–26E; PDP (Notification of Data Breaches) Regulations 2021

framework: Turkey Personal Data Protection Law (KVKK)
trigger: Controller learns that processed personal data was obtained by others through unlawful means — Board Decision 2019/10 sets a 72-hour backstop from learning of the breach.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Personal Data Protection Board (KVKK Kurulu)
authority: Personal Data Protection Board (KVKK Kurulu)
legal_reference: Law No. 6698 Art. 12(5); Board Decision No. 2019/10

framework: UK GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018 breach notification
trigger: Controller becomes aware of a personal data breach posing a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
authority: Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)
legal_reference: UK GDPR Art. 33/34; Data Protection Act 2018

framework: UK Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018
trigger: Operator of essential services or relevant digital service provider becomes aware of an incident with a significant impact on service continuity.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Sectoral competent authority (e.g. Ofcom, Ofgem, DHSC) and ICO for relevant digital service providers
authority: Sectoral competent authority (e.g. Ofcom, Ofgem, DHSC) and ICO for relevant digital service providers
legal_reference: NIS Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/506), reg. 11 and reg. 12(6)

framework: US Banking Agencies Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule
trigger: Banking organization determines a computer-security incident rises to a 'notification incident' materially disrupting operations, business lines, or financial stability.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Primary federal banking regulator (OCC, Federal Reserve, or FDIC)
authority: Primary federal banking regulator (OCC, Federal Reserve, or FDIC)
legal_reference: 12 CFR Part 53 (OCC), 12 CFR 225.300–303 (FRB), 12 CFR Part 304 Subpart C (FDIC)

framework: Colorado Security Breach Notification Law
trigger: Determination that a security breach of personal information likely occurred and misuse has occurred or is reasonably likely; AG notice required when 500+ Colorado residents affected.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Colorado Attorney General
authority: Colorado Attorney General
legal_reference: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 6-1-716

framework: Florida Information Protection Act (FIPA)
trigger: Determination of a breach of security of unencrypted personal information; Department notice required when 500+ Florida residents affected.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
authority: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
legal_reference: Fla. Stat. § 501.171

framework: Massachusetts Data Breach Notification Law
trigger: Knowledge of a breach of security or unauthorized use of personal information creating substantial risk of identity theft or fraud; notice due 'as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay' — no fixed hour backstop.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Massachusetts Attorney General and Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation (OCABR)
legal_reference: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93H, §§ 1–6; 201 CMR 17.00

framework: Texas Identity Theft Enforcement and Protection Act
trigger: Discovery of a breach of system security involving sensitive personal information of Texas residents; AG notice required electronically when 250+ residents affected.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Texas Attorney General
authority: Texas Attorney General
legal_reference: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 521.053

framework: Virginia Database Breach Notification Law
trigger: Discovery of unauthorized access and acquisition of unencrypted personal information causing or reasonably believed to cause identity theft or fraud; no fixed statutory hour deadline ('without unreasonable delay').
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Virginia Attorney General

framework: Washington State Data Breach Notification Law
trigger: Discovery of a breach of secured or unencrypted personal information of Washington residents; AG notice required when 500+ residents affected.
what_is_due: Initial notification to Washington State Attorney General
authority: Washington State Attorney General

framework: South Africa Protection of Personal Information Act
trigger: Reasonable grounds to believe personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person; notice due 'as soon as reasonably possible' — no fixed statutory deadline.
what_is_due: No fixed hour clock is modelled for this framework
authority: Information Regulator (South Africa)
legal_reference: POPIA s. 22
